newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian govt can work despite scandals -Maystadt.
newsitem.headline: Belgian govt can work despite scandals -Maystadt.

text.p: Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt said on Monday scandals surrounding one of the four partners in the centre-left ruling coalition did not prevent the government from functioning properly.

"It is not because one of the coalition parties is experiencing difficulties that the government is kept from functioning. I see no problem for the government as such," he told reporters after a meeting of EU Finance Ministers.
The main French-speaking partner in the coalition, the PS socialist party, said on Friday it had had contacts with two firms at the heart of allegations of illegal party financing.
The largest party in the coalition, the Flemish Christian Democratic party CVP, told the PS on Monday to get its act together to remain credible.
The so-called Dassault and Agusta scandals centre on claims the French and Italian companies of the same names bribed parties in the late 1980s to win lucrative defence contracts.
Both firms have denied any wrongdoing.

The CVP said it wanted to update the government programme ahead of next month's 1997 budget review and set priorities for the final two years of its legislature. "The most important criteria is whether this government can carry on with its work...we hope that the government can go on, but this assumes that the PS will continue to put things right internally."
"It remains to be seen whether the PS will be able to be a firm coalition partner," it said.
Maystadt belongs to the francophone Christian Democrats.
